items.title: Section: What Triggers Each Particular Factor, and Why Feeling Sometimes Belongs to the Eye and Sometimes to Thought

items.zh: 問：此不遍行五種心法，於何各別境事生耶？答：如其次第，於所愛、決定、串習、觀察四境事生。三摩地、慧，於最後境；餘隨次第，於前三境。問：諸名所攝與心相應所餘蘊法，當言率爾起耶？尋求耶？決定耶？答：若依彼類心，當言即彼類。
items.en:
Question: with respect to what particular objects do these five non-universal mental factors arise? Answer: in sequence, towards a beloved, a determined, a habituated, and an observed object. Concentration and wisdom arise towards the last; the rest, in sequence, towards the first three.
Question: should feeling, perception, and formations, associated with mind among the aggregates subsumed under name, be said to arise as initial mind, searching mind, or determining mind? Answer: whichever class of mind they depend on, they should be said to belong to that same class.

items.title: Section: Egg Yolk and Egg White — Why Mind and Its Factors Never Operate Separately

items.zh: 問：如經言：此四無色蘊，當言和合，非不和合，不可說言如是諸法可分、可析，令其差別。何故彼法異相成就，而說和合無差別耶？答：眾多和合，於所緣境受用領解方圓滿故。若不爾者，隨闕一種，於所為事應不圓滿。
items.en: Question: as scripture says, these four formless aggregates should be said to operate in combination, not otherwise, and one cannot say these phenomena can be divided or analysed apart when they arise. Why, then, do these phenomena each possess a distinct character, yet are said to combine without differentiation? Answer: only through the combination of many factors is an object fully experienced, received, and understood. Otherwise, lacking even one, the intended task would remain incomplete.

items.title: Section: Four Names for Mind and Its Factors — Having an Object, Being Associated, Having Activity, Having a Basis

items.zh: 問：諸心心法，凡有幾種差別名耶？答：有眾多名，謂有所緣、相應、有行、有所依等無量差別。問：何故眼等亦有境界，而但說彼名有所緣，非眼等耶？答：由彼眼等離所取境亦得生起，心與心法則不如是。問：何故名相應？答：由事等故、處等故、時等故、所作等故。問：何故名有行？答：於一所緣作無量種差別行相轉故。問：何故名有所依？答：由一種類託眾所依差別轉故。雖有為法無無依者，然非此中所說依義。唯恒所依為此量故。
items.en: Question: how many different names distinguish mind and its mental factors? Answer: countless names, among which are having an object, being associated, having activity, and having a basis. Why are they called associated? Because of shared object, shared basis, shared time, and shared task. Why are they called having activity? Because countless distinct activities occur upon a single object. Why are they called having a basis? Because this single category depends on multiple distinct supports in order to occur.

items.title: Section: Clarity and Ignorance, Cause and Fruit — And a Detour Through the Platform Sūtra's Thirty-Six Pairs

items.zh: 問：何故樂望苦受、苦望樂受、若樂若苦望非苦樂說互相對？答：由自種類而不同分互相對故。問：何故不苦不樂受望彼無明說互相對？答：由與諸受、一切煩惱皆為助伴互相對故。問：何故明與無明說互相對？答：能治、所治互相對故。問：何故明與涅槃說互相對？答：因果相屬互相對故。
items.en: Question: why are pleasant feeling and painful feeling, and pleasant or painful feeling and neutral feeling, said to stand in mutual contrast? Answer: because though of the same category, they occupy different positions within it. Question: why is neutral feeling said to stand in contrast to ignorance? Answer: because both serve as the constant companion of their own category. Question: why are clarity and ignorance said to stand in contrast? Answer: as remedy against what is remedied. Question: why are clarity and nirvāṇa said to stand in contrast? Answer: as cause against its fruit.

items.title: Section: The Tenth and Final Topic — Nine Angles on Wholesome, Unwholesome, and Neutral, and Six Grounds Where Goodness Arises

items.zh: 云何建立四無色蘊為善、不善、無記性耶？謂一切無差別。嗢拕南曰：依處、與自性、相應、世俗等、軟等、事、差別、德失、能所治。問：善法依處有幾種？答：略說有六。一、決定時，二、止息時，三、作業時，四、世間清淨時，五、出世清淨時，六、攝受眾生時。
items.en:
How are the four formless aggregates established as wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral? All follow the same framework without distinction. A mnemonic verse states: ground and essential nature, association and conventional status, grades of intensity, underlying basis, further distinction, gain and loss, and remedy and what is remedied.
Question: how many grounds does a wholesome state have? Answer: briefly, six — the moment of firm conviction, the moment unwholesome states are set aside, the moment of performing action, the moment of worldly purification, the moment of supramundane purification, and the moment of embracing other beings.

items.title: Section: Eleven Wholesome Factors — Faith, Shame, Modesty, and the Roots That Make Genuine Goodness Possible

items.zh: 問：何等為自性？答：謂信、慚、愧、無貪、無瞋、無癡、精進、輕安、不放逸、捨、不害，如是諸法名自性善。
items.en: Question: what is the essential nature of the wholesome? Answer: faith, moral shame, moral modesty, non-greed, non-hatred, non-delusion, diligence, pliancy, non-negligence, equanimity, and non-harming — these phenomena constitute wholesomeness by their own essential nature.

items.zh: 問：如是諸法互相應義，云何應知？

items.title: Section: The Rice Merchant's Riddle — How Faith Met the Moment of Firm Conviction

items.en: Answer: at the moment of firm conviction, faith accompanies it.

items.title: Section: Which Wholesome Factor Accompanies Which Moment — From Setting Aside Faults to Embracing Others

items.zh: 止息雜染時，有慚與愧，顧自他故。善品業轉時，有無貪、無瞋、無癡、精進。世間道離欲時，有輕安。出世道離欲時，有不放逸及捨。攝受眾生時，有不害，此是悲所攝故。
items.en: When unwholesome states are set aside, moral shame and moral modesty arise, having regard for self and other respectively. When wholesome action is performed, non-greed, non-hatred, non-delusion, and diligence arise. In worldly purification through freedom from desire, pliancy arises. In supramundane purification through freedom from desire, non-negligence and equanimity arise. In embracing beings, non-harming arises, this being subsumed under compassion.

items.zh: 問：是諸善法，幾世俗有？幾實物有？

items.title: Section: Three Merely Conventional Virtues, and What Makes a Wholesome Root Soft, Medium, or Superior

items.zh: 答：三世俗有。謂不放逸、捨及不害。所以者何？不放逸、捨是無貪、無瞋、無癡、精進分故。即如是法離雜染義，建立為捨；治雜染義，立不放逸。不害即是無瞋分故，無別實物。問：何等名軟善根？答：諸不定地所有善根；或在定地，而能對治上品煩惱。問：何等名中品善根？答：若在定地世間善根；或能對治中品煩惱。問：何等名上品善根？答：謂出世間所有善根；或能對治下品煩惱。又諸善法，或由加行力、或由串習力、或由自性力、或由田士力、或由清淨力，當知成上品。
items.en:
Answer: three exist conventionally — non-negligence, equanimity, and non-harming. Why? Non-negligence and equanimity are positional variants of non-greed, non-hatred, non-delusion, and diligence. This same phenomenon, in the sense of departing from defilement, is established as equanimity; in the sense of countering defilement, is established as non-negligence. Non-harming is simply a variant of non-hatred, without any separate reality.
Question: what is a soft wholesome root? Answer: any wholesome root belonging to an unsettled mind, or, even in a settled mind, one capable of countering only superior-grade affliction. Question: what is a medium wholesome root? Answer: worldly meditative wholesome roots, or those capable of countering middling affliction. Question: what is a superior wholesome root? Answer: supramundane wholesome roots, or those capable of countering subtle affliction. Furthermore, wholesome phenomena become superior through the power of effort, the power of habituation, the power of inherent tendency, the power of a worthy field, or the power of purification.

items.zh: 問：善根生時，依幾種事而得生耶？

items.title: Section: Eight Ways a Wholesome Root Actually Gets Started, From Generosity to Embracing Other Beings

items.zh: 答：若略說依八種事。一、施所成福業事，二、戒所成福業事，三、修所成福業事，四、聞所成事，五、思所成事，六、餘修所成事，七、簡擇所成事，八、攝受有情所成事。
items.en: Answer: briefly, eight kinds of activity. Merit accomplished through generosity, merit accomplished through moral discipline, merit accomplished through meditative cultivation, activity accomplished through learning, activity accomplished through reflection, activity accomplished through further cultivation, activity accomplished through discernment, and activity accomplished through embracing sentient beings.

blocks.text: Mind and its factors always work together, "like yolk and white". Then the eleven wholesome factors, beginning with faith.
Aspiration goes with the beloved, resolve with the determined, mindfulness with the habituated, concentration and wisdom with the observed.
Only through combination is an object fully experienced and understood. Master Cháng Bǎi: though each factor has its own character, they depend on one another.
Having an object, being associated, having modes of activity, having a basis. Master Cháng Bǎi: many factors act together with the mind on one object.
Clarity and ignorance, cause and fruit. Master Cháng Bǎi: clarity is the wisdom that counters affliction.
Master Cháng Bǎi: when there is firm conviction about worldly or supramundane good, wholesome states arise.
Master Cháng Bǎi: faith in false teachings does not purify the mind and is not good faith; non-hatred gives beings happiness.

subs.head: Faith at the moment of conviction

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi: deciding to ordain, for instance, is believing that monastic practice can lead out of the three realms; without firm conviction, one has no faith.
Pliancy goes with worldly freedom from desire; heedfulness and equanimity with the supramundane. Master Cháng Bǎi: embracing beings for one's own benefit is not wholesome.
Heedfulness, equanimity, and non-harming exist only as phases of other factors. Master Cháng Bǎi: they have no activity of their own.
Eight kinds of activity, beginning with giving. Master Cháng Bǎi: giving counters stinginess and gives rise to non-greed; acting for beings must come with non-hatred.
Faith in the Yogācāra sense is not belief without reason: it is the clarity that comes with firm conviction.

quiz.q: Towards what objects do the five non-universal factors arise?
options: aspiration towards the determined, resolve towards the beloved, mindfulness towards the observed, and concentration and wisdom towards the habituated
all five arise towards every object, just as the universal factors do, with no particular objects to speak of
aspiration towards the beloved, resolve towards the determined, mindfulness towards the habituated, and concentration and wisdom towards the observed
aspiration towards the past, resolve the present, mindfulness the future, concentration and wisdom all three
quiz.why: The treatise matches in order: aspiration with the beloved, resolve with the determined, mindfulness with the habituated, and concentration and wisdom with the observed. Master Cháng Bǎi: the objects of the particular factors each differ, unlike the universal factors, which take the same object. This is why they are also called object-specific.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi assign initial, searching, and determining minds to the consciousnesses?
options: initial mind is mental consciousness alone; searching and determining extend to the five
initial mind extends to the five and mental consciousness; searching and determining belong to mental consciousness
all three belong to the five alone, mental consciousness joining only from a fourth mind onward
all three belong to the store-consciousness
quiz.why: The treatise answers that feeling, perception, and formations belong to whichever class of mind they depend on. Master Cháng Bǎi: initial mind extends to the five sense-consciousnesses and mental consciousness, whereas searching and determining are the work of mental consciousness.

quiz.q: The four formless aggregates each have a distinct character. Why are they called combined without differentiation?
options: because the four are really one phenomenon with four names, and so cannot be analysed
only together can an object be fully experienced and understood; lacking one, cognition is incomplete
because the claim that each has its own character is wrong, as the treatise refutes, so no distinction is needed
because all four are form, and so without difference
quiz.why: The treatise answers that only through combination is an object fully experienced and understood; lacking one, the task is incomplete. Master Cháng Bǎi: though these many phenomena each have their own character, they depend on one another and function together, and only so is an object fully enjoyed. Distinct character and inseparable functioning are compatible.

quiz.q: "Having activity": the English has "countless distinct activities" for 差別行相. How does the lecture explain?
options: 行 means walking, the postures, since mind moves about, and "activities" rightly conveys this bodily action
行 means the formations aggregate, feeling and perception excluded
many factors act with mind on one object; 行相 are modes of the mind, of which "activities" takes only the side of acting
行 means practice, only practitioners having it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: so many different mental factors, on one object, manifest and act together with the mind, and so mind and factors are called having activity. 行相 are the modes in which they take the object, such as receiving or marking. "Activities" is serviceable, but it does not show that these are modes of apprehending one object.

quiz.q: How do clarity and ignorance, and clarity and nirvāṇa, stand in contrast?
options: clarity and ignorance as cause and fruit; clarity and nirvāṇa as remedy and what is remedied
both as different positions within one category, which is why the treatise illustrates them with feeling
clarity and ignorance as remedy and what is remedied; clarity and nirvāṇa as cause and fruit
both as companions
quiz.why: The treatise distinguishes kinds of contrast: within one category, as companions, as remedy and remedied, and as cause and fruit. Master Cháng Bǎi: clarity is the wisdom that counters afflictions, and ignorance the affliction countered; clarity is the wisdom severing afflictions, the cause of nirvāṇa, and nirvāṇa its fruit.

quiz.q: What are the six grounds of a wholesome state?
options: giving, discipline, patience, diligence, absorption, and wisdom, arranged according to the six perfections
seeing, cultivation, beyond learning, accumulation, application, and nirvāṇa
firm conviction, setting aside, performing action, worldly purification, supramundane purification, embracing beings
birth, ageing, sickness, death, abiding, and change
quiz.why: The treatise lists six moments on which wholesome states rest. Master Cháng Bǎi: when there is firm conviction regarding worldly or supramundane good, wholesome phenomena arise, and so the moment of conviction is a ground. The next section matches particular wholesome factors to each of these six.

quiz.q: Which eleven phenomena are wholesome by their own nature?
options: faith, diligence, mindfulness, concentration, wisdom, joy, pleasure, pliancy, equanimity, the awakening limbs, and the path limbs, in order of practice
the six perfections and the four immeasurables
faith, shame, modesty, non-greed, non-hatred, non-delusion, diligence, pliancy, non-negligence, equanimity, non-harming
not killing, stealing, and the rest of the ten good courses
quiz.why: The treatise names these eleven as wholesome by their own nature. Master Cháng Bǎi: faith in false teachings does not purify the mind or give rise to good, and cannot be called good faith; non-hatred gives beings happiness, and non-harming removes their pain. So faith is defined by what it does to the mind, not by mere believing.

quiz.q: "At the moment of firm conviction, faith accompanies it." What example does Master Cháng Bǎi use?
options: faith arises long after the decision, so one should ordain first and let faith come slowly, in that order only
deciding to buy rice is believing its price will rise
deciding to ordain is believing that practice brings release; with no firm conviction of its merit, one has no faith to ordain
deciding not to believe is the highest wisdom
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: deciding to ordain, for instance, is believing that monastic practice can lead out of the three realms, up to unexcelled awakening; without firm conviction about the merit of such practice, one has no faith to ordain. So faith and firm conviction go together, the one being the ground of the other.

quiz.q: What wholesome factors accompany freedom from desire on the worldly and supramundane paths?
options: pliancy on the worldly path; non-negligence and equanimity on the supramundane
non-negligence and equanimity on the worldly path; pliancy on the supramundane, since only noble ones can attain pliancy
shame and modesty on the worldly path; faith on the supramundane
non-harming on the worldly path; diligence on the supramundane
quiz.why: The treatise pairs pliancy with worldly freedom from desire, and non-negligence and equanimity with the supramundane. Master Cháng Bǎi: cultivating absorption and subduing desire, aversion, and harm, leaving coarse burden behind, one gains pliancy; on the supramundane path, leaving defilement is set up as equanimity, and countering defilement as non-negligence.

quiz.q: "In embracing beings, non-harming arises, subsumed under compassion." What caution does Master Cháng Bǎi add?
options: embracing beings is always good whatever the motive, so one need not examine one's resolve, only the number gathered
embracing beings for one's own benefit is not wholesome; non-harming is a phase of non-hatred, sparing beings pain
non-harming is a separate real phenomenon, unrelated to non-hatred
non-harming belongs to kindness, not compassion, so the treatise errs
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: embracing beings for one's own benefit is not a wholesome state. Non-harming is a phase of non-hatred; a person without hatred can be kind to beings, and not harming them spares them pain. So the wholesome quality lies in the compassionate mind, not in the outward fact of gathering people.

quiz.q: Which three of the eleven exist conventionally, and why?
options: faith, shame, and modesty, all three depending on others and lacking a nature of their own, and so conventional
pliancy, diligence, and non-delusion, all phases of wisdom
non-negligence, equanimity, non-harming; the first two are phases of non-greed, non-hatred, non-delusion, and diligence, the last of non-hatred
non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion, all names for wholesome roots
quiz.why: The treatise names non-negligence, equanimity, and non-harming. Master Cháng Bǎi: non-negligence and equanimity are phases of those four, with no activity apart from them; to exist conventionally is to be provisional, with no real substance of one's own, existing as a phase of other phenomena.

quiz.q: The English has "positional variants" for 分. Why is this addition good?
options: 分 means separation, these having their own reality apart from non-greed and the rest, as "positional" shows
分 means allotment, of practice time
分 here is a difference of phase, conventional things existing as phases of others; plain "part" would suggest a component
the addition is poor and should be deleted entirely
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: what exists conventionally has no real substance and exists as a difference of phase in other phenomena. "Positional variants" brings out this sense of 分位. A plain "part" would mislead, suggesting that non-negligence is a component of non-greed. The same word in §27 is only "variant," so the rendering could be made uniform.

quiz.q: 軟善根 counters 上品煩惱, which the English gives as "only coarse affliction," while §27 has "superior grade." How does this compare?
options: superior-grade affliction is subtlest, needing superior roots, so "coarse" reverses it and should be "subtlest"
上品 means the highest merit of affliction, and should be "best"
§19 and §27 speak of different afflictions, so two renderings are right
superior-grade affliction is coarsest, countered by soft roots; §19 gets the sense, but one term has two renderings and "only" is added
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: superior-grade afflictions are the coarser ones, and the root that counters them is of the soft grade; the affliction severed first is the most obvious and is called superior. So "coarse" gets the sense here, but the same term is "superior grade" in §27, and a reader may think the superior grade is the hardest to sever.

quiz.q: On which eight kinds of activity do wholesome roots briefly rest?
options: seeing suffering, origin, cessation, the path; cultivation, beyond learning, the worldly and supramundane paths, arranged by stage
the four mindfulnesses and four right efforts
merit of giving, discipline, and cultivation; activity of learning, reflection, further cultivation, discernment; and embracing beings
the noble eightfold path
quiz.why: The treatise lists eight kinds of activity. Master Cháng Bǎi: giving counters stinginess and gives rise to wholesome roots such as non-greed; and acting for beings' benefit must come with the compassion of non-hatred and non-harming, which is also a ground of the wholesome. Each activity serves as a remedy for some defilement, as the next section says.
